title: Hoydich Enterprises · Personal transit 2030
disclaimer: Independent design fiction. Architectural illustrations are not construction instructions or flight-certified blueprints. Hoydich Enterprises' El Segundo factory is an aspiration, not an existing facility. No flight performance, certification, partners or funding are claimed.
premise: A small personal cabin moves through a city that gives people more time. Ground transit does the ordinary work; a separately engineered aerial system is a question to investigate, never an assumed capability.

forms.name: Tidemark
forms.subtitle: Ground-first modular personal pod
forms.body: A quiet two-person cabin imagined on a low-speed ground platform. Explore accessible boarding, luggage, serviceability and an understandable interface before any aerial vehicle exists.
forms.uncertainty: Seats, dimensions and road approval require engineering; this is a visual proposition.
forms.alt: White two-seat ground pod with caramel seats beside a separate futuristic aerial carrier concept.
forms.caption: 2030 design study. Neither road nor flight approval is claimed. Aerial docking and failure handling remain unresolved.

forms.name: Stratus
forms.subtitle: Two-seat aerial form study
forms.body: A speculative personal aircraft silhouette with distributed propulsion. Study aircraft category, energy, noise and emergency landing needs as open questions with qualified engineers.
forms.uncertainty: No verified lift, range, speed, autonomy or airworthiness.
forms.alt: White and cobalt futuristic two-seat aircraft concept parked in a sunlit coastal aerospace hangar.
forms.caption: 2030 design study. Flight performance and aircraft classification have not been established; illustrated shrouds are not validated protection.

forms.name: Nimbus
forms.subtitle: Far-horizon personal cocoon
forms.body: What if a journey felt more like a protected chair than a car? A provocative single-seat form study, not the first manufacturing program. Human factors, noise, downwash, energy and failure tolerance remain unanswered.
forms.uncertainty: A speculative form, not a buildable or validated flight system.
forms.alt: Single-seat futuristic white transit cocoon displayed in a coastal design gallery beside an adult for scale.
forms.caption: 2030 design study. Neither occupant protection nor flight capability has been validated.

systems.name: Human cabin
systems.role: Boarding, restraints, accessibility, luggage and legible status.
systems.interfaces: Occupant needs → cabin geometry → ground and aircraft requirements.
systems.evidence: Accessibility studies and ergonomic mockups with human review.

systems.name: Structure & attachment
systems.role: Separate ground and aerial structural requirements; inspectable interfaces.
systems.interfaces: Loads, fatigue and crashworthiness requirements owned by qualified engineering teams.
systems.evidence: Analysis plans, materials records and independent structural review.

systems.name: Energy & thermal
systems.role: Investigate energy storage, thermal management and isolation.
systems.interfaces: Vehicle demands ↔ thermal system ↔ charging and fire response.
systems.evidence: Bench-only characterization and hazard assessment before vehicle integration.

systems.name: Propulsion research
systems.role: Compare plausible aircraft configurations without choosing performance numbers.
systems.evidence: Simulation review and contained ground test plans; no flight instructions.

systems.name: Safety & assurance
systems.role: Identify hazards, responsibilities, failure responses and evidence gaps.
systems.interfaces: All systems ↔ engineering review ↔ regulator-agreed compliance evidence.
systems.evidence: Requirements traceability, independent review and a documented go/no-go process.

systems.name: Human interface
systems.role: Clear state, manual operational responsibility and accessible explanations.
systems.interfaces: Human operator ↔ vehicle state ↔ service desk.
systems.evidence: Usability studies; no autonomy or aircraft-control software is supplied.

systems.name: Ground operations
systems.role: Maintenance, charging, inspection, dispatch and community impact.
systems.interfaces: Vehicle ↔ trained service team ↔ permitted infrastructure.
systems.evidence: Tabletop exercises, service procedures and a noise/community research plan.

systems.name: Digital record
systems.role: Trace parts, requirements, changes and evidence across the lifecycle.
systems.interfaces: Supplier documentation ↔ quality records ↔ human approval.
systems.evidence: Auditable records, limited access and security review; no flight-control connection.

factory.name: Design office
factory.body: Requirements, industrial design, community research and digital configuration control.

factory.name: Supplier interface
factory.body: Specify capabilities and qualification needs. Public directory entries are leads, not partners.

factory.name: Ground demonstrator cell
factory.body: Accessible mockups and non-flying integration studies with qualified supervision.

factory.name: Inspection studio
factory.body: Incoming inspection, traceability, calibrated measurement and documented nonconformances.

factory.name: Service school
factory.body: Design for repair; rehearse maintenance, emergency response and human handoffs.

factory.name: Certification branch
factory.body: An independently gated aviation program with regulator engagement before aircraft design commitments.

phases.goal: Choose a problem before a vehicle
phases.deliverable: User research, ground-first use case, category assessment and initial hazard register.
phases.gate: Qualified engineering and regulatory review of the intended use.
phases.funding: Founder-supported research or appropriately scoped research grants; eligibility unverified.

phases.deliverable: Full-scale non-flying cabin mockup, ground experience studies, supplier RFQs and a traceability prototype.
phases.gate: Human factors, accessibility, safety and cost review before powered integration.
phases.funding: Research collaborations, grants where eligible and negotiated development services; no partnerships assumed.

phases.deliverable: Independent trade study: ground product, aviation research or stop. Develop a regulator-engagement and compliance plan if aviation is selected.
phases.gate: Credible safety, community, financing and certification path; a stop decision is valid.
phases.funding: Private strategic financing only after professional legal and financial review; no offer is made here.

phases.goal: Build evidence, not a launch date
phases.deliverable: Qualified supplier program, reviewed ground integration and documented verification methods. Flight activity requires separate approved programs.
phases.gate: Independent safety assurance and applicable approvals before any aircraft test.
phases.budget: Aviation program cost is not estimated here; it may greatly exceed prior exploration budgets.
phases.funding: Milestone financing conditioned on evidence, realistic capital needs and applicable law.

phases.deliverable: Publish what was learned and decide whether any permitted ground product or separately certified aviation product is viable.
phases.gate: Certification, operational permission and production readiness are prerequisites, not calendar promises.
phases.budget: Production capital requires a new bottom-up estimate.
phases.funding: No funds are solicited, securities offered or prototype flight organized by this page.

budgetNotes: Numbers are fictional planning assumptions in 2026 USD, not quotes, forecasts, investment terms or a total aircraft-program budget. They exclude land, full aircraft certification, production tooling, insurance and operating infrastructure. Replace them with qualified bottom-up estimates before decisions.
openQuestions: Does a ground-only cabin solve the actual problem?
Who benefits, and who bears noise, cost and access burdens?
What aircraft category and operating model would apply?
What energy and emergency-response constraints rule out the concept?
Which supplier capabilities can be qualified and independently inspected?
What evidence would make us stop?
